name: Repeated measurement
summary: Repeating a (post-selected) Z-measurement several times is fault-equivalent to cutting the wire.
description: A wire on which the same $Z$-measurement (an X-spider with a one-legged Z-spider attached) is repeated three times is fault-equivalent to the wire cut into a $\langle +|$-effect and a $|+\rangle$-state. Semantically, already a single such measurement cuts the wire; under noise, the repetitions form detecting regions so that faults between them are detected. The thesis notes that the same holds for any number $n \geq 2$ of repetitions. Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1.
parameter_notes: Shown for n = 3 repetitions (the triple measurement of the thesis); holds for any n ≥ 2.
